docs.title: FungiTastic 🧫🍄
docs.text: FungiTastic is a Python toolkit designed for fungal image understanding, supporting tasks such as training classifiers, extracting features, computing similarities, and performing image retrieval or evaluation. It is designed to work with various fungal datasets and enables reproducible research in fungal taxonomy and visual recognition.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• 🔍 Support for local and global feature extraction
  • 🤝 Similarity computation for retrieval and classification
  • 🧪 Modular training, feature fusion, and evaluation pipelines
  • 📦 Ready-to-use for fungal identification and research tasks

docs.title: 🧪 Baselines & Models Overview
docs.text:
FungiTastic includes strong, diverse baselines for all benchmark tasks. You’ll find:

  • Ready-to-use pre-trained weights and scripts
  • Classic CNNs, modern transformers, and multimodal models
  • Results on all main benchmarks

docs.title: 📋 Model Categories
docs.text:
Task Model Page Baseline Types Closed-set Classification Closed-set Models CNN, ViT, BEiT, etc. Few-shot Learning Few-shot Models ProtoNet, NN, CLIP, etc. Open-set Classification Open-set Models Softmax, logit, DINOv2 Vision-Language Fusion VLM Fusion DistilBERT, Fusion

Segmentation models are covered in the Segmentation Baselines.

docs.title: 🏆 FungiTastic Benchmarks
docs.text: FungiTastic is designed to push the limits of machine learning in real-world biological classification through a comprehensive suite of benchmarks. These challenges reflect the unique, dynamic, and fine-grained nature of fungal data in the wild.

docs.title: Why Multiple Benchmarks?
docs.text:
• Realistic evaluation: Biological data are messy—seasonal, imbalanced, shifting, and full of new discoveries.
  • Diverse ML challenges: Tackle closed-set, open-set, few-shot, domain adaptation, segmentation, and more.
  • Multi-modal & cost-sensitive: Go beyond images, leverage metadata and context, and reason about real-world consequences (e.g., edible vs. poisonous).

docs.title: 🧩 Benchmark Tasks
docs.text:
Below is an overview of all the supported benchmarks. Click the task name to jump to the dedicated section and learn more about the data splits, evaluation metrics, and baseline results.

Task Description Link Closed-set Classification Standard fine-grained classification—species from a fixed set. Closed-set Open-set Classification Identify when an observation belongs to a new, unseen species. Open-set Few-shot Learning Recognize rare species with only a handful of training samples. Few-shot Chronological (Domain Shift) Handle distribution shifts—train/test splits follow real observation dates. Chronological Cost-sensitive Classification Penalize mistakes by their real-world impact (e.g., toxic/edible errors). Cost-sensitive Segmentation Detect and segment key body parts of fungi for fine-grained recognition. Segmentation

docs.title: 🔒 Closed-set Classification
docs.text:
• Goal: Assign the correct species label to each image from a fixed set of classes.
  • Highlights: Long-tailed, visually similar classes; strong baseline models provided.
  • 👉 Read more…

docs.title: 🌍 Open-set Classification
docs.text:
• Goal: Detect when a test observation is from a species not seen during training.
  • Use-case: New/rare fungi are continually discovered in nature—your model should know when it’s unsure.
  • 👉 Read more…

docs.title: 🎯 Few-shot Learning
docs.text:
• Goal: Correctly classify species with fewer than five training samples.
  • Highlights: Rewards ability to generalize from very little data—crucial for rare/under-observed species.
  • 👉 Read more…

docs.title: ⏳ Chronological / Domain Shift
docs.text:
• Goal: Evaluate robustness to distribution shift over time (e.g., due to seasonality, climate, or new locations).
  • Highlights: Train on older data, validate/test on newer years; reflects real-world deployment scenarios.
  • 👉 Read more…

docs.title: ⚖️ Cost-sensitive Classification
docs.text:
• Goal: Minimize "real-world" error costs. E.g., confusing a poisonous with an edible mushroom is much worse than the reverse.
  • Highlights: Supports research into non-standard losses and safety-aware AI.
  • 👉 Read more…

docs.title: ✂️ Segmentation
docs.text:
• Goal: Identify and segment morphological parts (caps, stems, gills, etc.) for selected species/groups.
  • Highlights: Supports interpretable and part-aware models, with hand-checked masks in the Mini subset.
  • 👉 Read more…

docs.title: 🗃️ FungiTastic Dataset
docs.text: FungiTastic is a large-scale, multi-modal benchmark dataset for computer vision, machine learning, and biodiversity research, centered around wild fungi observations. It offers expert-labeled data across more than 5,000 species, collected over 20+ years, and is designed to power research in fine-grained recognition, domain adaptation, multi-modal learning, open-set recognition, and more.

docs.title: 🚀 What’s Inside?
docs.text:
• Size: ~350,000 observations, >600,000 images, ~5,000 species.
  • Modalities: Photographs, satellite data, climate time series, segmentation masks, expert taxon labels, rich metadata, and image captions.
  • Expert Curation: Species labels are expert-verified; a subset includes DNA-sequenced ground truth.
  • Region: Predominantly Denmark and Northern Europe.
  • Time span: 2003–2023.

docs.title: 🧑‍🔬 What Can You Use It For?
docs.text:
FungiTastic is specifically designed to benchmark and develop advanced ML models for:

  • Fine-grained image classification (closed-set, open-set)
  • Few-shot learning and rare species recognition
  • Multi-modal and multi-task learning (combine visual, tabular, geospatial, and textual data)
  • Domain adaptation and temporal shift (study seasonal, habitat, and year-to-year distribution changes)
  • Vision-language modeling (with detailed image captions)
  • Semantic and instance segmentation
  • Cost-sensitive classification (e.g., recognizing poisonous vs. edible species)

See the Benchmarks section for a deep dive on supported challenges.

docs.title: 📚 Dataset Subsets
docs.text: FungiTastic is split into several subsets, each tailored for different research tasks:

docs.title: 1. FungiTastic (Full)
docs.text:
• The main benchmark set: >346k observations, >4,500 species, with all modalities.
  • Use: Closed-set & open-set classification, multi-modal modeling.

docs.title: 2. FungiTastic-Mini (FungiTastic–M)
docs.text:
• A compact subset from 6 challenging genera (e.g., Russula, Amanita, Boletus).
  • Includes body part segmentation masks for ~70k images.
  • Use: Fast prototyping, segmentation, few-shot, open-set.

docs.title: 3. FungiTastic–FS (Few-shot)
docs.text:
• Observations from species with <5 training samples.
  • Use: Few-shot learning & rare species recognition.

Details and statistics for each subset are provided in the Subsets and Benchmarks pages.

docs.title: 🔗 Available Data Modalities
docs.text:
Each observation can include a combination of:

  • Photographs & Captions: High-quality images (incl. some spore micrographs) and automatic detailed text descriptions.
  • Taxonomic Labels: Full biological hierarchy and toxicity (edible/poisonous).
  • Body Part Segmentation Masks: For toadstool-type fungi in the Mini subset.
  • Tabular Metadata: Date, location, habitat, substrate, elevation, land cover, etc.
  • Remote Sensing Data: 64x64 multi-band satellite images at 10m spatial resolution.
  • Climate Time Series: 20 years of temperature/precipitation data and bioclimatic variables.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Biological data are not i.i.d.—they change over time due to seasonality, climate, and location. FungiTastic’s temporal splits let you test robustness to domain shifts.

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
• Domain adaptation, continual learning, and test-time adaptation research
  • Models deployed in changing or dynamic environments

docs.title: Data & Splits
docs.text:
• Train: Observations up to 2021
  • Validation: Observed in 2022
  • Test: Observed in 2023
  • Splits follow real-world chronology, including natural class and distribution shifts

docs.title: Evaluation Protocol
docs.text:
• Metrics: Standard classification metrics (Top-1, F1) or task-specific as appropriate
  • Can be applied to closed/open/few-shot tasks

docs.title: Baselines & Results
docs.text:
• Baselines demonstrate substantial accuracy drops across years
  • Encourages research into robust, adaptive models

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
• See usage/evaluation.md for scripts and analysis
  • Download temporal splits from Kaggle

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The classic supervised task: Given an image, assign it to one of the species present in the training set. This is especially challenging in FungiTastic due to its fine-grained labels, long-tailed class distribution, and domain shifts.

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
• Automated fungal species identification for field guides, citizen science apps, etc.
  • Baseline for comparing closed-world vision models.

docs.title: Data & Splits
docs.text:
• Uses the main FungiTastic split: training (all data up to end of 2021), validation (2022), test (2023).
  • Only species present in the training set are evaluated.

docs.title: Evaluation Protocol
docs.text:
• Primary Metric: Top-1 accuracy
  • Secondary Metrics: Macro F1-score, Top-3 accuracy

docs.title: Baselines & Results
docs.text:
State-of-the-art models (e.g., ResNet, EfficientNet, ViT, BEiT) are provided as benchmarks. - Transformer architectures outperform classic CNNs, but all models struggle due to dataset complexity.

See Baselines & Models for scripts and results.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
• Download split files from Kaggle.
  • Use usage/training.md for a quickstart on model training.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Not all mistakes are equal! In FungiTastic, confusing a poisonous species for an edible one can have severe consequences, whereas the reverse is less dangerous. This benchmark evaluates models under custom loss/cost functions that reflect real-world priorities.

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
• Safety-critical systems (e.g., mobile ID for foragers)
  • Research into cost-sensitive, risk-aware, or calibrated classifiers

docs.title: Data & Splits
docs.text:
• Uses standard FungiTastic splits (temporal)
  • Poisonous/edible labels and additional risk metadata provided

docs.title: Evaluation Protocol
docs.text:
• Metrics: Weighted error rates, custom cost matrices (see Appendix in the paper)
  • You may define your own costs for specific errors

docs.title: Baselines & Results
docs.text:
• Example: False positive edible has high penalty; false positive poisonous has lower penalty
  • See example code and detailed description in Baselines & Models and evaluation protocols

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
• Use provided cost matrix and baseline scripts
  • Extend to new tasks with your own risk functions

docs.title: Related
docs.text: • Closed-set Classification

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Rare species are the norm, not the exception! The few-shot benchmark isolates species with fewer than five training samples. The task: Can your model generalize with minimal supervision?

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
• Identification of rare, endangered, or newly observed fungi
  • General few-shot learning research (prototypical networks, embedding-based methods, etc.)

docs.title: Data & Splits
docs.text:
• Only species with <5 training images are included.
  • Standard temporal splits: train (up to 2021), validation (2022), test (2023).

docs.title: Evaluation Protocol
docs.text:
• Primary Metric: Top-1 accuracy
  • Secondary Metrics: Macro F1-score, Top-3 accuracy

docs.title: Baselines & Results
docs.text:
Includes nearest-neighbor, centroid-prototype, and standard classifiers on strong feature extractors (CLIP, BioCLIP, DINOv2, BEiT).

See Baselines & Models for results and example code.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: • Few-shot split provided in the dataset package and Kaggle.

docs.text:

  • Closed-set Classification

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Real-world fungal datasets are never closed: New and previously unseen species appear in the wild each year. The open-set benchmark asks: Can your model detect when a specimen belongs to an unknown class?

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
• Discovering new or rare species
  • Deployed models that must avoid confident mistakes on out-of-distribution data

docs.title: Data & Splits
docs.text:
• Training: Species up to end of 2021.
  • Validation: Contains species first observed in 2022.
  • Test: Contains species first observed in 2023.
  • "Unknown" label is used for new classes.

docs.title: Evaluation Protocol
docs.text:
• Primary Metric: Area Under ROC Curve (AUC)
  • Secondary Metric: True Negative Rate @ 95% True Positive Rate (TNR95)

docs.title: Baselines & Results
docs.text:
Includes Max Softmax Probability, Max Logit Score, and Nearest Mean approaches, evaluated on both supervised and pre-trained (DINOv2, BEiT) backbones.

Detailed results and code: Baselines & Models

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Accurate segmentation of fungal body parts (caps, gills, stems, etc.) is crucial for fine-grained recognition and interpretability. FungiTastic–Mini includes part segmentation masks for a subset of species.

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
• Automated species identification pipelines
  • Explainable AI and morphological analysis
  • Training and evaluating segmentation models on natural data

docs.title: Data & Splits
docs.text:
• FungiTastic–Mini: Images with expert-checked segmentation masks
  • Classes: cap, gills, pores, ring, stem (and background)
  • Split: train/val/test following Mini subset

docs.title: Evaluation Protocol
docs.text:
• Semantic Segmentation: mean Intersection over Union (mIoU)
  • Instance Segmentation: mean Average Precision (mAP)

docs.title: Baselines & Results
docs.text:
• Baseline: Zero-shot pipeline (GroundingDINO + SAM)
  • Baseline IoU: ~89% (but misses small/atypical parts)
  • Further improvements possible with domain-specific models

See Baselines & Models for details.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
• Download Mini subset and annotation masks
  • Use sample notebooks/scripts in usage/training.md

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Each photo in FungiTastic includes a detailed, automatically generated caption describing visual features relevant for identification.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
• Generated by: Malmo-7B Vision-Language Model
  • Description Focus: Color, shape, texture, size of the fungi and its parts.
  • Prompt: Tailored to avoid speculation, highlight identification-relevant details.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
• Provided as a field in the metadata for each image.
  • Enables vision-language and multi-modal research.
  • Useful for text-only classification and fusion models.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: "The image shows three mushrooms in a grassy area. They have white stems and light brown caps. Their caps are dome-shaped..."

docs.title: Learn More
docs.text:
• Photographs for images linked to captions.
  • VLM Fusion Models for downstream uses.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Each observation comes with 20 years of historical climate data for its location, supporting distribution modeling and temporal studies.

docs.title: What’s Included
docs.text:
• Monthly values: Mean, min, max temperature, total precipitation.
  • Bioclimatic variables: 19 features (e.g., seasonality), averaged over 1981–2010.
  • Coverage: Data up to 2020 for all observations; newer obs may have missing final years.

docs.title: Data Source
docs.text: • Extracted from CHELSA and other open-access climate datasets.

docs.title: Usage Notes
docs.text:
• Format: time series per observation (CSV or torch tensor).
  • Missing years for 2020–2024 observations are noted in the data.

docs.title: Learn More
docs.text:
• See Metadata for site locations and environment.
  • See Satellite Data for environmental context.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A subset of FungiTastic (Mini) includes expert-verified segmentation masks for key morphological parts of fungi.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
• Available for: FungiTastic–Mini images (6 genera, ~70k photos).
  • Categories: Cap, gills, pores, ring, stem, background.
  • Annotation: Human-corrected, generated with Segment Anything Model (SAM) + manual QA.
  • Format: PNG mask per image or torch tensor.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
• Supports semantic and instance segmentation benchmarks.
  • Enables interpretable recognition and morphological analysis.

docs.title: Learn More
docs.text:
• Segmentation Benchmark
  • Photographs for source images.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Every FungiTastic observation comes with rich tabular metadata describing not just the specimen, but also its context and collection details.

docs.title: Fields Included
docs.text:
• Observation date: yyyy-mm-dd, plus year, month, and day columns.
  • EXIF camera metadata: exposure, color space, device type, etc.
  • Habitat: E.g., Mixed woodland, Deciduous woodland (32 options).
  • Substrate: Where the specimen grows (e.g., Bark, Soil, Stone).
  • Taxonomic labels: Full hierarchy from species up to kingdom.
  • Toxicity status: Edible or poisonous (binary label).
  • Geolocation: Latitude, longitude, plus region/district/country.
  • Biogeographical zone: Atlantic, Continental, Alpine, etc.
  • Elevation: Standardized meters above sea level.
  • Land cover: Classification from MODIS (e.g., savanna, barren).

docs.title: Usage Notes
docs.text:
• Nearly all observations (>99.9%) have full metadata.
  • Metadata is crucial for multi-modal learning, habitat modeling, and context-aware classification.

docs.title: Learn More
docs.text:
• See Photographs & Captions for image links.
  • See Climate Data and Satellite Data for further contextual attributes.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: FungiTastic provides multi-band satellite image patches for nearly all European observation sites. These images capture the environmental context around the specimen.

docs.title: Data Details
docs.text:
• Type: 64×64 pixel image patches, 10m spatial resolution.
  • Bands: Red, Green, Blue, Near-infrared (NIR), Elevation, Land cover.
  • Source: Sentinel-2A, Ecodatacube, ASTER, ESA WorldCover.

docs.title: File Format
docs.text:
• Provided as torch tensors with shape [6 × 64 × 64] per patch.
  • Each observation is centered on its location.

docs.title: Usage Notes
docs.text: • Useful for remote sensing research, species distribution modeling, and combining with in-situ photos.

docs.title: Learn More
docs.text:
• Metadata for location and land cover info.
  • Climate Data for long-term weather variables.

docs.title: 🧪 Evaluation Protocols
docs.text: Accurate, fair evaluation is key to FungiTastic! This page explains how to evaluate your models for all main benchmarks, including metrics, submission format, and leaderboard suggestions.

docs.title: 1. Standard Metrics
docs.text: Task Main Metric(s) Closed-set Classification Top-1 Accuracy, Macro F1, Top-3 Accuracy Open-set Classification AUC, TNR@95%TPR Few-shot Learning Top-1 Accuracy, Macro F1 Segmentation mIoU, mAP Cost-sensitive Custom weighted loss, see below

docs.title: 2. How to Evaluate
docs.text:
• Use the provided *_test.csv files for each benchmark.

  • After inference, output a CSV:

    • For classification: image_id,predicted_label
    • For open-set: add a column for is_unknown or use "unknown" as a label
    • For segmentation: follow COCO or Pascal VOC format

  • Python example (classification): 

    import pandas as pd
from sklearn.metrics import f1_score, accuracy_score

y_true = [...]  # ground-truth labels
y_pred = [...]  # your predictions

print("Accuracy:", accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred))
print("Macro F1:", f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average="macro"))

  • Open-set: Use ROC/AUC and TNR metrics, see Open-set Models

docs.title: 3. Cost-sensitive Evaluation
docs.text:
• Download or define a cost matrix: higher penalties for dangerous mistakes (e.g., poisonous predicted edible).
  • Use sample code from Baselines & Models or Appendix A in the paper.

docs.title: 4. Submitting to Leaderboards
docs.text:
• For official challenges or leaderboards, see instructions in README or GitHub Issues.

Need more? Check Benchmarks for protocol details or open an issue!

docs.title: 🏋️ Training Your Model on FungiTastic
docs.text: This page gives practical steps to get started training a model for any FungiTastic benchmark.

docs.title: 1. Setup
docs.text:
• Clone the repo and install requirements: 

    git clone https://github.com/bohemianvra/FungiTastic.git
cd FungiTastic
pip install -r requirements.txt

  • Download the dataset (see Downloading the Dataset).

docs.title: 2. Loading the Data
docs.text:
• Each benchmark split is a CSV/TSV file listing image paths and metadata.

  • Example (Python/pandas): 

    import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("fungitastic/closed_set_train.csv")
print(df.columns)  # See available metadata fields

  • Images are typically stored as paths in the DataFrame. Load with your favorite library (PIL, OpenCV, etc).

docs.title: 3. Training Scripts & Examples
docs.text:
• Example scripts for closed-set, few-shot, open-set, and segmentation are in examples/ in the repo.
    • E.g., examples/train_closed_set.py
  • All baselines use standard PyTorch; configs and hyperparameters are in the paper and README.

docs.title: 4. Tips
docs.text:
• Always start with the Mini subset for fast prototyping.
  • For multi-modal training (images + metadata), see the relevant examples.
  • Use pre-trained weights as strong starting points—see Baselines & Models.

docs.title: 5. Extending to New Benchmarks
docs.text:
• FungiTastic is benchmark-agnostic: write your own splits, add modalities, or propose new tasks.

Next steps: - Evaluation Protocols - Baselines & Models
